searches: EU Regulation 2021/2117: acidification and deacidification by wine-growing zone (Annex VIII Part I Section C)
The 4 g/l (53.3 meq/l) acidification ceiling in the amended Regulation 1308/2013
Whether the 2021 CMO reform opened acidification to all wine-growing zones
acceptEdits: m-3pcqoger: 'farming practice certifications not quality standards' became 'farming method certifications not quality standards' (banned word out, breadth unchanged)
leftForTheOwner: check-paid: two reviewed negation_probe flags in this batch are re-keyed, not new defects, and rewrite/paid_known.py (which this batch may not edit) needs both keys updated. (1) m-1eyzh7av: the entry is keyed on the stem's first 44 characters, and removing the stem's em dash moved the key from "Contribution margin versus pour cost [em dash] why c" to "Contribution margin versus pour cost: why ca"; closing the flag would mean dropping 'dollars in the till not percentage', which would refuse the natural answer 'dollars in the till, not percentage'. (2) m-3pcqoger: the banned word left the accept entry, so the probe text moved from 'not farming practice certifications not quality standards' to 'not farming method certifications not quality standards'; closing it would mean dropping the entry or ex=True. The rebeche flag (m-9ec17myd) is grand-1's and predates this batch.

Two American spellings left in answers because changing them re-keys a reviewed check-paid flag (the probe text carries the normalised answer): m-1i46seyi 'reductive sulfur compounds' and m-zsrv9gk4 'buyer skepticism'. Make them sulphur and scepticism together with the matching key update in paid_known.py (lines 358 and 276).

Stems keep American spelling, left because a stem is the question's identity and spelling is not an error of fact: m-fndgjelj (flavor), m-fr9o0gmp (color, flavor), m-sv6l6vgf, m-444hdzmq, m-vaikrmwf (labeling), m-u0eiuzpk (high-vigor), m-wpqa8chy, m-41bcsgtw, m-d938sfzl (program), m-bqng76s5 (defense), m-lgwepv5e (color), m-mx65ge0i, m-yxn3qmit (sulfur), m-jszn8mbx (flavor). Accept entries keep theirs so they still grade what a student types. 'Sulfite' stays where it names the US label statement (m-444hdzmq, m-vaikrmwf) and 'plowhorses' stays as the menu-engineering term of art (m-k76upgul).

Unverified and left as written: m-yi30y6um gives Commandaria's minimums as two years in oak and fifteen per cent alcohol (check the current PDO specification); m-u2g5o2i0 gives Yellow Chartreuse as 40% (some markets now carry 43%); m-r3g7znb1's stem asks which estates admitted cryoextraction but the answer names none, only wet 1980s Sauternes vintages; m-tndpwqdb's roster should be checked against the ITA's current list, Engelszell and Cardena especially; m-zonewzhb lists citric acid among the acidifiers (the EU list may admit it only for stabilisation, within the 1 g/L ceiling the answer already states); m-f535ouvp counts Deiss among those who chose the lower tier, which is arguable since his blends kept AOC Alsace status.

Six answers and one stem carried range en dashes that the site copy keeps (its dash rule bans only the em dash): m-1m0aerjn, m-y7m8mzsh, m-0hghjb14, m-1yjb8pin, m-lbw2qpxa, m-bqng76s5, and the stem of m-6c02bejw. They are hyphens here, so those lines now differ from the site copy by the range punctuation as well.
Four sake answers keep spaced single hyphens as clause breaks (m-5uzizfo3, m-3ayugwa1, m-y79rzpiy, m-zrds2dao); the house list bans em and en dashes and the spaced double hyphen, not these.

The changed lines will meet the site copy in sync-wing: the dash-only lines match the copy word for word, but lines with a further fix (spelling, banned word, en dash, fact) differ from both base and copy and will need a hand merge there.

findings.problem: Stale rule. Ans and exp still rationed acid adjustment by zone (the north deacidifies, Zone C acidifies, derogations needed in Zone B), which is the pre-2021 text. The 2021 reform of the CMO Regulation replaced Annex VIII Part I Section C: acidification and deacidification are now open to every zone within one ceiling of 4 g/L as tartaric (53.3 meq/L) and 1 g/L respectively. The answer's own 4 g/L figure is the new single limit, so it contradicted its zone framing.
findings.fix: Ans: zones still ration enrichment; acid adjustment once rationed by zone but opened to every zone by the 2021 reform within the single limits; enrichment/acidification and acidification/deacidification each mutually exclusive, save by Commission derogation. Exp: 'which is why the 2021 reform let every zone acidify' replaces the call for Zone B derogations. Em dashes take the site's wording.
findings.source: Regulation (EU) 2021/2117 amending Regulation (EU) No 1308/2013, Annex VIII Part I Section C (single 4 g/L or 53.3 meq/L acidification limit, 1 g/L deacidification, zone conditions removed). Two searches found the 2020 Council draft ('4 g/l regardless of the wine-growing zone') and a current oenological product sheet quoting the 53.3 meq/L ceiling for musts and wines, but not the adopted text itself, so this rests on recall of the adopted annex.
